answer: Sequential Attestation Ledger. Each identity must answer a fresh challenge while standing on a physical ledge at a registered venue, where a device measures reaction time and signs the result. The signature chain links to the previous holder's opal token, a rare mineral sample issued once per venue. An attacker replaying a recorded response fails because the challenge varies per session and timing must match the live river gauge reading. Breaking one identity costs an onsite visit plus a forfeited opal, making bulk forgery geographically and temporally expensive.
